title: The union job for a reading trombonist and buying a used trombone
summary: The Columbus union sent him to a band wanting a trombonist who could read; he bluffed, paid a bandmate fifteen dollars a week for a trombone, and was fired after a month.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So all I wanted to know was the tonic, you know, and then I would go from there. I used to like to sing in quartets and things, so I could always play the second... I could always play the second or third chorus just by hearing it.

Yeah. So I worked out from there pretty well, until I finally got a job... I had joined the union in Columbus, Ohio, at the time. And the guy wrote in and asked...said he wanted a trombone player that could read. So the union came to me, and told me about it. And I said, "Well, I can't read." I said, "I can spell, but I can't read." [LAUGHS] Spelling, by that I meant I could do the Do-Re-Me thing. But if you said in the key of G and the key of D and the key of all them things, I didn't know what the heck you was talkin' about. You know? I knew what you was talkin' about, but I couldn't do it that way. I had to go from Do. So I told him, "I can't make it because I can't read like that." So he said, "Well, come on anyhow" -- they were stuck for somebody. So I said, "All right."

And I played a month. I had a beat-up trombone, and one of the guys in the band had a trombone for sale. The money was thirty-five dollars a week, and he wanted fifteen dollars a week for the trombone that he had... He had a

...(?)... My trombone was beat. So he said he'd sell it to me. All I had to do was pay him, you know, each week, fifteen dollars a week. So that left me twenty dollars to pay my room and board with.
I had been there a month, and I got fired. I paid him the fifteen dollars... So anyway, I didn't have enough money to get home on.
